current_answer: As of 27 September 2026, public evidence still does not establish a broad decline in popular models’ core capability. GPT-6 Sol has a negative Bug Hunt coding slice, but Braintrust’s separate 175-example API evaluation is nearly tied; both are cross-sectional tests with different tasks and setups. OpenAI’s 25 September Codex outage was a declared availability event, not a quality test. RoboHarm’s results page reports different refusal and task-completion rates for GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 robot-agent policies, but its public repository does not include raw rollouts or a frozen results dataset for independent recalculation. The robot-policy comparison does not test either model over time or ordinary chat. Retry after a declared incident, then replay the same task on the same surface with model identity, route, settings, tools, context, budget, and final artifact recorded.

catalogue_card.question: Are popular AI models getting worse right now?
catalogue_card.text: No broad decline is proven. A negative coding slice and a near-tied API test disagree; a new robot-safety result measures another system, not model change over time.

summary: No broad cross-model core-capability decline is proven.
Bug Hunt reports GPT-6 Sol at 29.3/105 versus GPT-5.6 Sol at 43.5/105 on a small, cross-sectional coding slice.
Braintrust reports a near-tie for GPT-6 Sol and GPT-5.6 Sol across 175 API examples; its task and setup differ from Bug Hunt and production surfaces.

RoboHarm’s results page reports 2 safety refusals, 97 purposeful attempts, and 60 task completions for its GPT-6 Astra robot policy across 100 trials; its public repository does not include raw rollouts or a frozen results dataset for independent recalculation.
OpenAI’s 25 September Codex outage was a service-availability event and was marked recovered.
The 27 September r/ClaudeAI hub requests task receipts, but its traffic claim is unquantified and its linked report summary is dated 21 September.
After a declared incident, retry or wait. Then replay one fixed task on the same surface and inspect the artifact before switching.
uncertainty: Bug Hunt is cross-sectional; the GPT-6 Sol and GPT-5.6 Sol comparison has small run counts, wide spread, different cost kinds, and an unverified context-accounting detail for the Sol control.
Braintrust reports 175 API examples across seven task families; top score differences overlap and the API harness, effort, judge, and task mix do not represent Work, Codex, or consumer Chat.

RoboHarm used five fixed unsafe instructions, one wording per instruction, 20 trials per policy-task cell, and one robot setup; its cross-sectional policy comparison cannot establish that a model changed over time or transfer to chat surfaces.

Robocurve’s public repository says raw rollouts and a frozen results dataset are not bundled, which prevents independent recalculation from that package; independent replication was not located in this run.
The Codex status record establishes a declared outage and provider recovery, not account-level task quality or post-recovery performance.
Community problem reports are self-selected. The current r/ClaudeAI hub claims high traffic but publishes no traffic count; its linked category summary was last dated 21 September, not 27 September.
There is no representative fixed-task series across Chat, Work, Codex, API, and competing providers with served identity, route, settings, tools, context, budget, artifact, judge, and denominator.
Analytics, a human pilot, a provider ledger, a recovered-work measure, and willingness-to-pay evidence remain unavailable.
freshness_note: Fresh public-source research completed 27 September 2026. RoboHarm adds a reported embodied safety result, but the repository does not provide raw results for independent recalculation and the policy comparison is cross-sectional; the broad-decline verdict is unchanged.
